overview: ANZ Group Holdings is one of Australia's 'Big Four' banks and the non-operating holding company for Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Limited (ANZBGL), formed via a 2024 restructure. The Group provides retail, commercial and institutional banking services across Australia, New Zealand and the Pacific, with a significant institutional/markets franchise across Asia. Fiscal year ends 30 September; the September 2025 half saw major restructuring charges, and FY2026 is dominated by the integration of the Suncorp Bank acquisition (completed mid-2025) and delivery of a newly announced 'ANZ 2030' strategy under new CEO Nuno Matos.

business_model.summary: ANZ earns net interest income by taking deposits and extending loans (mortgages, business and institutional lending) funded at a margin, plus non-interest fee and trading income from transaction banking, markets/FX, and wealth-adjacent products. The FY2025/H1 FY2026 divisional cash profit mix is led by Institutional (~35% of cash profit), Australia Retail (~25%), New Zealand (~21%), Business & Private Bank (~18%), and Suncorp Bank (~7%), net of a negative Group Centre contribution from treasury/central items and one-off costs.

revenue_streams.name: Institutional markets, FX and transaction banking fees
Retail/commercial fees and other operating income

business_model.customer_type: Mixed: mass-market retail/mortgage customers (B2C, ~8m+ Australian retail plus ~1.26m Suncorp Bank customers), SME/commercial (Business & Private Bank), and large corporate/institutional/government clients across Australia, NZ and Asia (B2B)
business_model.geographic_mix: Australia (Retail, Business & Private Bank, Suncorp Bank, and the Australian arm of Institutional) is the largest segment; New Zealand is a full-service #1-ranked market-leading franchise; Institutional also spans Asia-Pacific, Europe and the Americas; total FTE split roughly Australia 47%, New Zealand 17%, Rest of World 36% (Mar-26)

main_competitors: Non-bank/fintech mortgage lenders and mortgage brokers
competitive_position.market_position: One of Australia's Big Four oligopoly banks; a top-4 major bank in Australian retail and commercial banking (post-Suncorp acquisition), the #1 institutional bank across Australia and New Zealand by relationship strength, and the #1 market leader in New Zealand banking overall

moat_factors.description: APRA banking licensing, capital and prudential requirements create very high barriers for new entrants; the Big Four control the large majority of Australian banking system assets
Large balance sheet (~A$1.31tn total assets) and strong credit ratings (Aa2/AA-/AA-) provide low-cost wholesale funding access versus smaller banks and non-banks
#1 relationship-strength ranking in Australia/NZ corporate banking and recognised leadership in transaction banking (Transactive Global platform) create switching costs for large corporate clients
197-year heritage brand; combined with Suncorp Bank, ANZ now serves over 11 million customers, though brand trust has been dented by recent regulatory/conduct issues
#1 market position in NZ banking provides a diversified, historically higher-returning profit pool outside the hyper-competitive Australian mortgage market

weaknesses: Australia Retail and Business & Private Bank divisions are underperforming peers amid intense mortgage-market price competition and broker channel dominance (~78% of new lending via brokers)

Elevated and unresolved non-financial risk (NFR) failures have triggered an APRA enforceable undertaking, a $1bn capital add-on, and an ASIC penalty, damaging trust and consuming management bandwidth and cost
Commoditised, low-differentiation mortgage product invites margin compression versus non-bank lenders and smaller competitors
Complex legacy technology stack (still being migrated to ANZ Plus) increases operating costs and execution risk relative to more digitally mature peers such as CBA

growth_drivers: ANZ 2030 strategy (announced October 2025) targeting materially improved productivity, growth and returns across four pillars: Customer First, Simplicity, Resilience and Delivering Value

Suncorp Bank integration accelerated to complete by June 2027 (from a longer original timeline), adding ~1.2m customers and ~A$47bn of home loans and lifting Queensland mortgage market share to ~15%, expected to unlock cost and revenue synergies as systems consolidate

ANZ Plus digital platform rollout, migrating all ~8 million Australian retail customers (and eventually Suncorp customers) onto a modern digital banking platform by September 2027, aimed at lowering the cost-to-serve and improving retail competitiveness

Organisational simplification and cost-out program (including ~3,500 planned FTE reductions and reduced third-party/contractor spend by September 2026) targeting a lower cost base and improved efficiency ratio
Institutional and transaction banking momentum (Transactive Global platform, #1 relationship-strength rankings) continuing to be a high-return, capital-light growth engine
New Zealand franchise continuing to perform well as a stable, high-returning profit pool
Renewed executive team (new CEO, Group CRO, Group CIO, Group Executive Australia Retail, Group Executive Operations) intended to drive faster execution and better risk management

business.description: Intense price competition and broker-channel dominance are compressing Australia Retail margins despite loan and deposit growth
Accelerated migration timeline to June 2027 carries operational, customer-experience and cost risk; total integration costs guided at ~A$745m, with ~A$200m/year expected in FY26-FY27
Markets and trading income can be volatile quarter to quarter and sensitive to client risk appetite and rates volatility
Large residential mortgage book (Australia Retail + Suncorp + NZ) concentrates credit risk in the domestic housing cycle

financial.description: NIM was 1.53% in H1 FY2026 (statutory), roughly flat to down versus prior periods, reflecting competitive deposit and lending pricing and a lower-rate environment
APRA's A$1bn operational risk capital add-on (up from A$750m) remains in place until remediation is delivered to APRA's satisfaction, constraining capital otherwise available for buybacks/growth
Significant NZD and USD earnings exposure requires ongoing economic hedging; debt issuance (~A$160bn) exposes the Group to wholesale funding market conditions

regulatory.risk: APRA Court Enforceable Undertaking / non-financial risk remediation
regulatory.description: ANZ entered a CEU with APRA in April 2025 after significant NFR management failures; APRA approved ANZ's Root Cause Remediation Plan in November 2025, with independent reviewer Promontory monitoring progress (first report released May 2026); the $1bn capital add-on persists until remediation is judged complete
September 2025 ASIC settlement of $240m in penalties across Australia Markets and Australia Retail (subject to Federal Court approval) highlights ongoing conduct and compliance risk

ANZ received a second 'strike' on its remuneration report at the December 2025 AGM (32.4% against, following a 38% first strike in 2024), reflecting sustained shareholder dissatisfaction, though a board-spill motion was heavily defeated
Ongoing APRA capital, leverage and liquidity requirements (CET1 12.4% at Mar-26, LCR 132%, NSFR 115%) constrain capital flexibility and require continual management

macro.description: RBA and RBNZ rate movements directly affect net interest margin and mortgage/deposit competition dynamics
A downturn in house prices or broader economic activity would pressure credit quality, loan growth and impairment charges across the large mortgage and business loan books

macro.risk: Geopolitical/trade tensions affecting Asian institutional franchise
macro.description: Institutional division's Asia exposure (including the PT Panin equity-accounted investment in Indonesia, impaired A$285m pre-tax in the Sep-25 half) is sensitive to regional economic and political conditions

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Australian and New Zealand banking remains an oligopolistic, well-capitalised, regulated industry; system credit growth is moderate and mortgage competition remains intense, while institutional/transaction banking and wealth-adjacent fee income offer better growth and return profiles
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high; bank earnings are sensitive to the credit cycle, interest rate cycle and housing market conditions in Australia and New Zealand; credit impairment charges remain low by historical standards (0.07% of average gross loans and advances in H1 FY2026) but can rise sharply in a downturn
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High; net interest margin and net interest income are directly affected by RBA/RBNZ policy rates, yield curve shape, and deposit/lending competitive dynamics
key_input_costs: Technology/software investment and integration spend (Suncorp migration, ANZ Plus)
Regulatory compliance and remediation costs (NFR uplift program)

recent_developments.event: Stock trading around A$36-37, near 52-week highs, with market cap ~A$108bn as of the March 2026 half-year end; total shareholder return of 10.7% for the March 2026 half and 15.1% for FY2025

H1 FY2026 results: statutory profit A$3,650m (flat YoY), cash profit A$3,780m (+6% YoY), CET1 ratio improved to 12.4%; proposed interim dividend of 83 cents per share (75% franked), up from 70% franking in the prior interim
Independent reviewer Promontory released its first report on progress against ANZ's APRA-approved Root Cause Remediation Plan for non-financial risk

ANZ received a second 'strike' on its remuneration report at the AGM (32.36% against votes), following a first strike in 2024; a subsequent board-spill resolution was heavily defeated (86.6%-98.6% against)
APRA approved ANZ's Root Cause Remediation Plan (RCRP) under the April 2025 Court Enforceable Undertaking

FY2025 full-year results: statutory profit A$5,891m (-10% YoY), cash profit A$5,787m (-14% YoY), cash EPS 194.7c (-29.6c), cash ROE 8.1% (-160bps), CET1 12.0% (-20bps); flat total dividend of 166 cents

New CEO Nuno Matos (joined May 2025, succeeding Shayne Elliott) unveiled the 'ANZ 2030' strategy at an October Strategy Day, built on four pillars (Customer First, Simplicity, Resilience, Delivering Value), alongside new appointments to the Executive Committee (Group Executive Australia Retail, Group Executive Operations, Group CRO, Group CIO)

September 2025 half significant items totalling ~A$1,316m pre-tax: PT Panin equity investment impairment (A$285m), staff redundancy program targeting ~3,500 departures by Sept-26 (A$585m), ASIC settlement of A$240m in penalties plus costs (A$271m total), accelerated Suncorp Bank migration costs (A$97m), and Cashrewards goodwill impairment/closure (A$78m)

ANZ announced it would bring forward full integration of Suncorp Bank (completing migration onto ANZ systems) to June 2027, ahead of the original schedule, with total integration costs guided at ~A$745m

ANZ ceased the remaining ~A$800m of its share buyback program to conserve capital for restructuring, technology investment and Suncorp integration; announced return of ~A$1bn surplus capital from its Non-Operating Holding Company

ANZ entered into a Court Enforceable Undertaking with APRA following the Oliver Wyman review into non-financial risk management weaknesses; APRA's operational risk capital add-on was subsequently increased to A$1bn

guidance.as_of: H1 FY2026 Results (May 2026) / FY2025 Annual Report (November 2025)

items.target: ~A$745m total, ~A$200m/year in FY26 and FY27, small residual in FY28
items.notes: Timeline brought forward to complete migration by June 2027 (from a later original date); ~A$300m incurred to date as of the FY25 update

items.target: Migrate all ~8 million Australian retail customers onto ANZ Plus
items.notes: Described as a core element of the ANZ 2030 strategy's 'resequencing'; foundational technology largely built

items.target: ~3,500 employee departures; reduced engagement of ~1,000 managed services contractors
items.notes: Announced September 2025 as part of bank simplification; FTE already down from 42,590 (Mar-25) to 40,072 (Mar-26)

items.target: 1.5% discount on DRP, expected to continue subject to capital position
items.notes: Applied following cessation of the on-market buyback; ~A$1bn of surplus NOHC capital returned to the operating bank

items.target: Phase 1 (FY26-FY27): fix fundamentals/productivity; Phase 2: accelerate growth and outperform market
items.notes: No explicit numeric revenue/EPS targets disclosed in the extracted filings for the multi-year strategy; management has flagged 'material growth over the next five years' as the ambition

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Paul O'Sullivan and CEO Nuno Matos both characterised FY2025 as a challenging reset year, with the profit decline attributed to significant items tied to conduct/regulatory remediation and business simplification rather than underlying deterioration. Management highlighted improving H1 FY2026 momentum (cash profit +6% YoY, CET1 up to 12.4%) as early evidence the ANZ 2030 strategy and cost-reduction program are taking hold, while cautioning that Australia Retail and Business & Private Bank divisions remain below where management wants them amid competitive mortgage pricing.

bull_case: Oligopoly banking structure in Australia/NZ with high regulatory barriers to entry supports durable, above-cost-of-capital returns over the cycle once remediation costs roll off
New CEO and largely refreshed executive team/board provide a credible reset narrative, with early H1 FY2026 results (cash profit +6% YoY, CET1 improving) supporting the turnaround thesis

Suncorp Bank integration, once completed by June 2027, should deliver cost synergies and scale benefits (Queensland mortgage share ~15%), while ANZ Plus migration lowers the long-run cost-to-serve in Australian retail

Diversified earnings base: the #1 New Zealand franchise and a leading institutional/transaction banking business (Transactive Global) partially offset a weaker Australian retail/commercial performance
Strong capital position (CET1 12.4%) and credit ratings (Aa2/AA-/AA-) provide balance sheet resilience and capacity to resume capital returns once the APRA capital add-on is lifted
bear_case: Non-financial risk failures remain unresolved: APRA's Court Enforceable Undertaking, a A$1bn capital add-on, and ongoing independent monitoring (Promontory) signal execution and reputational risk could persist for years
Two consecutive AGM 'strikes' on remuneration highlight sustained shareholder distrust in management/board accountability, raising governance overhang risk

Australia Retail and Business & Private Bank divisions continue to underperform amid intense mortgage-market competition and broker-channel dominance, with no clear numeric turnaround targets yet disclosed
Suncorp Bank integration acceleration to June 2027 raises near-term execution and customer-experience risk, with ~A$745m of integration costs to be absorbed through FY2028
FY2025 cash profit fell 14% and cash ROE dropped 160bps to 8.1%, and further one-off/remediation charges could recur as the multi-year NFR uplift program continues
